title: Shop Floor Clock & Multi-Job Tracking
brief: Wire ShopFloorClockPage and related components (ShiftClockWidget, ActiveJobsDashboard, JobSelector) to real backend data from TimeClockEngine. Adds handoff notes, fatigue alerting, enhanced pause reasons, barcode job selection, WebSocket real-time updates with polling fallback, and offline IndexedDB queue. Depends on BIZ-MS0 completing the jobTimePause route fix and TimeClockEngine enhancements.

phases.title: Enhanced Shift Clock + Job Tracking Wiring
phases.description: Wire ShiftClockWidget and ActiveJobsDashboard to the enhanced TimeClockEngine backend, adding handoff notes, fatigue alerting, pause reason categories, and production count capture on job stop.

units.title: Wire ShiftClockWidget to enhanced backend

steps.instruction: Read web/src/components/jobs/ShiftClockWidget.tsx in full to understand existing state and props
Add getShiftHandoff(employeeId: string) to web/src/api/client.ts — GET /api/erp/shift-handoff/:employeeId, returns { handoff_notes: string, operator_name: string, clock_out_time: string } | null
On clock-in render: call getShiftHandoff() for the current employee and display the previous shift's handoff_notes in a yellow banner if present (operator name + time + notes)
On clock-out: show a textarea (min 3 rows, placeholder 'Handoff notes for next operator...') and pass handoff_notes value to shiftClockOut() call
Add fatigue alert banner: if current shift duration >= 12 hours, render a red banner 'FATIGUE ALERT: 12+ hours on shift. Consider a break.' above the clock-out button
Ensure clock-out button is disabled while the handoff_notes textarea is empty (require at least 1 non-whitespace character)
Run npm run build:fast and fix any TypeScript errors

deliverables.description: ShiftClockWidget with handoff notes input, previous handoff display, fatigue alert banner

exit_conditions: Clock in shows previous operator's handoff notes in yellow banner if available
Clock out prompts for handoff notes (required, non-empty)
Fatigue alert banner appears at 12+ hours on shift
getShiftHandoff() makes correct GET call and handles null response
abort_criteria: BIZ-MS0 not complete (TimeClockEngine lacks handoff_notes on ShiftEntry)
shiftClockOut route does not accept handoff_notes parameter
units.rollback: Revert ShiftClockWidget.tsx to last working commit; remove getShiftHandoff from client.ts

units.title: Wire ActiveJobsDashboard to enhanced job tracking

steps.instruction: Read web/src/components/jobs/ActiveJobsDashboard.tsx in full to understand existing job card structure and state
Add process_type selector to each job card: a small segmented control with values [setup, run, rework, inspection, teardown] — default from job routing data, operator can change
Ensure the live job timer is displayed in 48px+ font on each job card, updating every second via setInterval
Add cost-so-far display on each job card: elapsed_seconds * (hourly_rate / 3600), formatted as '$XX.XX', updating every 30 seconds

Replace single pause button with 5 quick-reason buttons on pause: machine_down (wrench icon), tool_change (gear icon), material_shortage (box icon), break (coffee icon), waiting_inspection (eye icon), plus an 'Other' button that opens a text input. Each sends reason_category + optional notes to jobTimePause()

Add stop button completion modal: number pad input for good_parts (large digit display, min 0), scrap_count input, scrap_reason dropdown [dimension_out_of_spec, surface_finish, wrong_material, operator_error, machine_fault, other]. Call jobTimeStop() with good_parts, scrap_count, scrap_reason, process_type

Add auto-pause toast: when user clicks Start New Job and there is already an active (running) job, show a toast 'Auto-pausing [job X] to start [job Y]' and call jobTimePause() on the running job with reason_category='break' before starting the new one
Update jobTimePause() call in web/src/api/client.ts to send { jobTimeId, reason, reason_category, notes? } in request body
Run npm run build:fast and fix any TypeScript errors

deliverables.description: ActiveJobsDashboard with process_type selector, 48px timer, cost-so-far, 5-reason pause buttons, completion modal with production counts
jobTimePause() updated to send reason + reason_category

exit_conditions: Each job card shows process_type selector, 48px+ live timer, cost-so-far
Pause shows 5 quick-reason buttons + Other with free text
Stop modal captures good_parts (number pad), scrap_count, scrap_reason
Auto-pause toast fires and pauses running job when starting a new one
jobTimePause API call sends reason_category in body
abort_criteria: BIZ-MS0 TimeClockEngine jobPause() does not accept reason_category
BIZ-MS0 jobStop() does not accept good_parts / scrap_count
units.rollback: Revert ActiveJobsDashboard.tsx to last working commit; revert jobTimePause signature in client.ts

scrutiny_focus: UX: 72px+ touch targets for all buttons on tablets
Fatigue alert: correct 12-hour threshold calculation accounting for pause periods
Pause reasons: all 5 categories map correctly to TimeClockEngine reason_category enum
Number pad: good_parts cannot be negative
Auto-pause: must not auto-pause an already-paused job

phases.title: Barcode Job Selection + Real-Time Updates
phases.description: Wire JobSelector with barcode scanner support and process type auto-selection from routing, then add WebSocket real-time multi-tablet sync with 10-second polling fallback.

units.title: Wire JobSelector to enhanced routing

steps.instruction: Read web/src/components/jobs/JobSelector.tsx in full to understand current job search and selection flow

Add a hidden <input type='text' autoFocus className='sr-only' /> at the top of the component for USB barcode scanner keyboard emulation — captures rapid keystrokes ending in Enter as a barcode scan event

On barcode scan (input receiving 4+ chars within 100ms followed by Enter key): call getJobByBarcode(barcode) API and populate the job selector with the result, showing a brief 'Job scanned: [job_number]' flash toast
Add getJobByBarcode(barcode: string) to web/src/api/client.ts — GET /api/erp/jobs/barcode/:barcode, returns JobSummary with job_number, description, process_type from routing, machine_id from routing

When a job is selected (by barcode or dropdown), auto-populate process_type from job routing (using the first unstarted operation). Show a confirmation step: 'Process: [setup/run/etc] — Confirm or change?'

Add machine_id selector dropdown populated from MachineRegistry — filtered to machines with matching process_type capability. Update jobTimeStart() call in client.ts to send process_type and machine_id in body
Run npm run build:fast and fix any TypeScript errors

deliverables.description: JobSelector with hidden barcode input, auto-populated process_type from routing, machine_id selector
getJobByBarcode() and updated jobTimeStart() with process_type + machine_id

exit_conditions: USB barcode scanner keystrokes captured by hidden autoFocus input
Barcode scan auto-populates job, process_type, machine_id from routing
Operator sees confirmation step before committing process_type
Machine dropdown shows only compatible machines for the process type
jobTimeStart() sends process_type and machine_id in request body
abort_criteria: No /api/erp/jobs/barcode/:barcode route exists on backend (would need BIZ-MS0 or separate unit)
MachineRegistry not accessible from frontend API
units.rollback: Revert JobSelector.tsx; remove getJobByBarcode from client.ts; revert jobTimeStart signature

units.title: Add WebSocket real-time updates + polling fallback

steps.instruction: Create web/src/hooks/useJobStatusSocket.ts — a React hook that opens a WebSocket to ws://[host]/api/erp/ws/job-status and subscribes to job_update events filtered by employeeId or departmentId
The hook returns { jobs, connectionStatus: 'connected' | 'polling' | 'disconnected', lastUpdated }. On WS message, parse JSON and update jobs state via React state dispatch
Implement 10-second polling fallback: when WS is closed or errors, set a setInterval that calls getActiveJobs() every 10 seconds. Clear interval when WS reconnects
Add exponential backoff reconnect to WebSocket: 1s, 2s, 4s, 8s, max 30s. Do not reconnect if component is unmounted (track with useRef isMounted flag)

Add connection status indicator to ShopFloorClockPage.tsx: a small dot (12px circle) in top-right corner — green (#22c55e) = WebSocket live, yellow (#eab308) = polling, red (#ef4444) = disconnected. Tooltip on hover shows 'Live' / 'Polling (Xs)' / 'Offline'

When any operator on another tablet pauses, resumes, or stops a job, the WS broadcast should cause the receiving tablet's ActiveJobsDashboard to re-render within 2 seconds. Verify this by reading the WS server broadcast logic in src/routes/erp.ts
Replace the existing polling in ActiveJobsDashboard (if any) with the useJobStatusSocket hook
Run npm run build:fast and fix any TypeScript errors

deliverables.description: WebSocket hook with polling fallback, exponential backoff reconnect, connection status

exit_conditions: WebSocket connects and receives job_update events
Polling fallback activates within 2 seconds of WS disconnect
Connection status dot shows correct color for each state
Two tablets see each other's job state changes within 2 seconds
Exponential backoff prevents reconnect storm
No memory leaks: intervals and WS closed on component unmount
abort_criteria: No WebSocket server endpoint exists at /api/erp/ws/job-status in erp.ts
WS server does not broadcast on pause/resume/stop events
units.rollback: Remove useJobStatusSocket.ts; revert ActiveJobsDashboard to direct API calls; remove status dot from ShopFloorClockPage

scrutiny_focus: Barcode scanner: hidden input must not steal focus from visible inputs
WebSocket: no reconnect storm — exponential backoff enforced
Polling fallback: interval must clear when WS reconnects to prevent double-update
Memory safety: all intervals and WS closed on unmount
Multi-tablet: broadcast must include enough data for full re-render (not just a ping)

phases.title: Offline Resilience
phases.description: IndexedDB offline queue for all shop floor actions, with automatic replay on reconnect and a pending-sync banner.

units.title: Add offline resilience with IndexedDB queue

steps.instruction: Create web/src/lib/OfflineQueueManager.ts — a class that wraps IndexedDB (idb or native IDBDatabase) with an 'offline_actions' object store. Schema: { id: auto-increment, action_type: string, payload: object, timestamp: ISO string, status: 'pending' | 'syncing' | 'failed' }
Implement enqueue(action_type: string, payload: object): Promise<number> — stores the action with status='pending' and returns the IDB key

Implement replayAll(): Promise<{ replayed: number, skipped: number, failed: number }> — iterates pending actions oldest-to-newest (sorted by timestamp), calls the corresponding API function for each action_type, marks as 'syncing' during the call. On 409 Conflict (already processed on server), mark status='skipped'. On success, delete the record. On other errors, mark status='failed' and stop replay
Implement getPendingCount(): Promise<number> and subscribe(callback: (count: number) => void) for reactive UI updates

Wrap the API functions in client.ts (shiftClockIn, shiftClockOut, jobTimeStart, jobTimePause, jobTimeStop) with a try/catch: on network error (fetch throws or status >= 500 and not 409), call offlineQueueManager.enqueue(action_type, payload) and return a synthetic optimistic response so the UI does not block

Create web/src/hooks/useOfflineSync.ts — subscribes to OfflineQueueManager.subscribe(), triggers replayAll() when navigator.onLine becomes true (via 'online' event), exposes { pendingCount, isSyncing }

Add pending-sync banner to ShopFloorClockPage.tsx: when pendingCount > 0, show a yellow banner at top 'X actions pending sync — will auto-sync on reconnect'. When isSyncing, show 'Syncing X actions...' with a spinner
Run npm run build:fast and fix any TypeScript errors

deliverables.description: IndexedDB offline queue with enqueue, replayAll, getPendingCount, subscribe
React hook wrapping OfflineQueueManager with online event listener and auto-replay
API wrappers updated to enqueue on network failure

exit_conditions: WiFi drop during pause: action queued in IndexedDB, UI shows 'X actions pending sync'
On reconnect: replayAll() fires automatically, banner shows 'Syncing...' then clears
If server returns 409 (already processed): record skipped without re-sending
Actions replayed in chronological order (oldest first)
getPendingCount() returns 0 after successful replay
OfflineQueueManager works in browsers supporting IndexedDB (Chrome 80+, Safari 14+)
abort_criteria: Target browsers do not support IndexedDB (extremely unlikely in 2026)
Server does not return 409 on duplicate action replay (conflict detection requires server-side idempotency keys)
units.rollback: Remove OfflineQueueManager.ts and useOfflineSync.ts; revert client.ts wrappers; remove banner from ShopFloorClockPage

scrutiny_focus: IndexedDB: object store created before first enqueue (handle onupgradeneeded correctly)
Replay order: must be strictly chronological, not insertion order if timestamps differ
Optimistic response: UI must not crash if API is unavailable — synthetic response must match shape of real response
Online event: 'online' fires on reconnect but network may not be fully ready — add 2s delay before replay
Failed replay: stop on first non-409 error to prevent partial state corruption

hook.name: biz-ms1-offline-guard
hook.description: Warn if API client function is added without a corresponding offline-queue enqueue call for shop floor action types

mcp_action.description: Fetch the most recent handoff notes for a given employee's last completed shift — used by ShiftClockWidget on clock-in render

skill_enhancement.enhancement: Touch-first tablet patterns: 72px targets, barcode scanner hidden input, offline-first API wrappers with IndexedDB queue, WebSocket + polling hybrid real-time

enforcement.build_gate: npm run build:fast must pass after each unit before proceeding to next unit
enforcement.no_mock_data: All API calls must target real backend routes — no fixture JSON or hardcoded arrays in completed units
enforcement.touch_targets: All interactive elements must be minimum 72px tall for tablet use
enforcement.offline_required: API wrappers for clock-in, clock-out, job start, pause, stop MUST have offline queue fallback after U-BIZ11
enforcement.websocket_fallback: WebSocket implementation must include polling fallback — pure WS with no fallback is not acceptable
enforcement.no_passthrough: No .passthrough() in any Zod schema added or modified in this milestone

Clock out requires and saves handoff notes
Fatigue alert banner appears at 12+ hours
Each job card shows: process_type selector, 48px+ live timer, cost-so-far
Pause presents 5 reason buttons + Other free text
Stop modal captures good_parts and scrap_count
Barcode scan auto-populates job + process_type + machine_id
Two tablets see each other's job changes within 2 seconds via WebSocket
Polling fallback activates on WS disconnect
WiFi drop queues action in IndexedDB, auto-syncs on reconnect
